item.title: France Is Veering Toward a Potential Debt Crisis, a Warning to the World
item.description: French bond investors are demanding sharply higher interest rates, a cautionary development for other high-debt countries.
item.dc:creator: Eshe Nelson
item.media:description: France’s fiscal turmoil highlights the risks facing heavily indebted governments as borrowing costs rise and public spending on health care, pensions and defense grows.

item.title: Oil Prices Jump on Outburst of Violence in the Middle East

item.dc:creator: Lisa Friedman and Jenny Gross

item.title: Amex Supersizes Newark Airport Centurion Lounge Before It Even Opens
item.description: To meet skyrocketing demand, lounge operators like American Express are racing to build bigger, and the Centurion in Newark’s Terminal A will be a giant.
item.dc:creator: Christine Chung
item.media:description: The 26,000-square-foot Centurion Lounge at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, currently American Express’s largest location, will take second place to the new one set to open at Newark Liberty International Airport next year.

item.title: The Little-Noticed Exception in Trump Accounts
item.description: Wealthy donors and companies can donate individual stocks to the new investment accounts for millions of children. That has raised legal questions.

item.media:description: President Trump, center, announces the rollout of Trump accounts, stock portfolios for children seeded with a one-time federal contribution.

item.title: Trump’s White House Ban on CNN, Politico and MS Now: What to Know
item.description: A judge temporarily blocked the president from barring journalists from White House grounds, but they are being excluded in other ways.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wemple
item.media:description: President Trump has barred CNN and a Politico reporter from traveling with him on Air Force One.

item.title: Can Your College Affect Your Income?
item.description: A new analysis of federal earnings data measures how much students who received federal financial aid earned four years after graduating. Our graphics reporter Arfa Momin studied the data to see when a graduate’s major and college mattered most to earnings.
item.dc:creator: Arfa Momin, Nour Idriss, Rafaela Balster and Edward Vega

item.title: How the Trump Administration Is Eroding Airline Passengers’ Rights
item.description: Under Sean Duffy, the Transportation Department has worked to roll back consumer protections. Passenger advocates say the changes favor airlines.
item.dc:creator: Christine Chung
item.media:description: During President Trump’s second term, the Department of Transportation has, among other things, dropped an initiative to force airlines to pay customers cash for some flight disruptions.

item.title: A Top Fed Official Casts Further Doubt on a Rate Rise This Month
item.description: The Federal Reserve is poised to raise interest rates further as it seeks to tame inflation, but that is unlikely to happen until the end of the year.
item.dc:creator: Colby Smith
item.media:description: Christopher J. Waller, a Federal Reserve governor, last month. In a speech on Thursday, he said that “there is some flexibility” about when to raise interest rates again.

item.title: At Nearly $300,000, Some Recent Duke Graduates Out-Earned All Their Peers
item.description: Federal data show Duke math majors earning a bigger median income four years after graduation than any other majors from any school. It’s a small cohort.
item.dc:creator: Ron Lieber

item.title: Trump Administration Investigates Wells Fargo for Race-Based Lending

item.dc:creator: Rob Copeland
item.media:credit: An Rong Xu for The New York Times

item.title: Fed Minutes Show Officials Saw More Work to Do to Quell Inflation

item.title: 6 Broken Bathrooms Force Flight to Make an Urgent Landing
item.description: An American Airlines flight was diverted to New York on Tuesday because of an “inadequate number of operational lavatories” — two, on a plane that normally has eight.

item.media:description: An American Airlines flight between Madrid and Dallas made an unscheduled landing in New York on Tuesday because most of its bathrooms were not working.

item.title: Why Markets Are Buoyant — and Under Pressure

item.title: Tishman Speyer Takes Over Chrysler Building With Big Renovation Plans

item.title: Europe’s Trade Tensions With China Are Coming to a Head

item.media:description: A car from BYD, China’s largest electric-vehicle maker, at an auto show in Munich last year.

item.title: Airfares Have Spiked. Is the Death of Spirit Airlines to Blame?
